quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During a troop campsite assignment, a new Scout from a different background is excluded from a patrol cooking group and overheard being mocked. As an upstander living the Scout Oath and Scout Law, what should you do first?
quiz_item.question: During a troop campsite assignment, a new Scout from a different background is excluded from a patrol cooking group and overheard being mocked. As an upstander living the Scout Oath and Scout Law, what should you do first?
options: A. Stay quiet so you do not create awkwardness with the older Scouts in the patrol.
B. Step in respectfully as an upstander, invite the new Scout into your group, make sure they feel welcomed and heard, and involve your Patrol Leader or adult leadership if harassment continues.
C. Post about the argument on social media after the campout.
D. Tell the new Scout to camp alone at the edge of the site so the patrol does not argue.
choices: A. Stay quiet so you do not create awkwardness with the older Scouts in the patrol.
B. Step in respectfully as an upstander, invite the new Scout into your group, make sure they feel welcomed and heard, and involve your Patrol Leader or adult leadership if harassment continues.
C. Post about the argument on social media after the campout.
D. Tell the new Scout to camp alone at the edge of the site so the patrol does not argue.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Step in respectfully as an upstander, invite the new Scout into your group, make sure they feel welcomed and heard, and involve your Patrol Leader or adult leadership if harassment continues.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Citizenship in Society emphasizes ethical leadership, welcoming others, and acting as an upstander rather than a passive bystander when a fellow Scout is excluded.
